overview: This dry run covers the cell membrane and transport across it. The material does not specify the energy source for active transport or provide examples of transported substances.

topics.title: Cell membrane structure and permeability
topics.summary: The cell membrane is a selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer.

topics.title: Diffusion
topics.summary: Diffusion moves particles down a concentration gradient.

topics.title: Active transport
topics.summary: Active transport requires energy and moves substances against a concentration gradient.

questions.question: What is the structure and permeability of the cell membrane?
questions.answer: It is a selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer.

questions.question: In which direction does diffusion move particles?
What are the two defining features of active transport described in the notes?
questions.answer: It requires energy and moves substances against a concentration gradient.

script: Let’s review cell transport. The cell membrane is a selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer, meaning the notes describe it as a barrier with selective permeability. Diffusion moves particles down a concentration gradient. In contrast, active transport requires energy and moves substances against a concentration gradient. Remember the contrast: diffusion moves down the gradient, while active transport moves against it and requires energy. The notes do not specify the energy source or give examples of substances transported.
